'''Keon Tyrese Ellis''' (born January 8, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida SouthWestern State College|Florida SouthWestern Buccaneers]] and the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]].

==High school career==
Ellis played basketball for [[Eustis High School]] in his hometown of [[Eustis, Florida]] before transferring to [[Leesburg High School (Leesburg, Florida)|Leesburg High School]] in [[Leesburg, Florida]] for his junior season.<ref>{{cite web |last=Perper |first=Jake |title=Keon Ellis talks first state title, summer with Team MOAM and more |url=https://www.prephoops.com/2017/06/keon-ellis-talks-first-state-title-summer-team-moam/ |website=Prep Hoops |access-date=November 13, 2021 |date=June 16, 2017}}</ref> He led Leesburg to back-to-back Class 6A state titles.<ref>{{cite web |last=Jolley |first=Frank |title=Next Level: Ellis' play on hardwood earns offer from Alabama |url=https://www.dailycommercial.com/story/news/local/eustis/2020/02/13/next-level-ellis-play-on-hardwood-earns-offer-from-alabama/1719774007/ |website=[[Daily Commercial]] |access-date=November 13, 2021 |date=February 12, 2020}}</ref> As a senior, Ellis averaged 12.7 points, 11 rebounds and two assists per game, helping his team achieve a 29–1 record.<ref name="hall">{{cite web |last=Hall |first=Erik |title=Keon Ellis: 3 things to know about the Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball guard |url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/sports/college/2021/03/18/keon-ellis-14-facts-alabama-basketball-guard-stats-quando-rondo/4744756001/ |website=[[The Tuscaloosa News]] |access-date=November 13, 2021 |date=March 18, 2021}}</ref> He signed to play college basketball for [[Gardner–Webb Runnin' Bulldogs men's basketball|Gardner–Webb]] but instead opted to join [[Florida SouthWestern State College|Florida SouthWestern]], a [[junior college]] program, for academic reasons.<ref>{{cite web |last=Cruse |first=Hunter |title=Taking Chances: Keon Ellis' path to Tuscaloosa |url=https://www.crimsoncrossover.com/post/taking-chances-keon-ellis-path-to-tuscaloosa |url-status=dead |access-date=November 13, 2021 |website=Crimson Crossover |archive-date=November 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211113191749/https://www.crimsoncrossover.com/post/taking-chances-keon-ellis-path-to-tuscaloosa }}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at Florida SouthWestern, Ellis averaged 8.3 points and three rebounds per game, earning Second Team All-[[Suncoast Conference]] honors.<ref name=hall/><ref>{{cite web |title=2018-19 Men's Basketball Awards |url=http://thefcsaasports.com/sports/mbkb/2018-19/men-s_basketball_awards |website=NJCAA Region 8 |access-date=November 13, 2021}}</ref> On January 4, 2020, he scored a school-record 41 points in a 92–77 win against [[St. Petersburg College]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ellis Scores School Record 41 to Lead FSW Over St. Pete |url=https://www.fswbucs.com/sports/mbkb/2019-20/releases/20200104tg8szm |website=Florida Southwestern College Athletics |access-date=November 13, 2021 |date=January 4, 2020}}</ref> In his sophomore season, Ellis averaged 18.1 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 2.1 steals per game, setting program single-season records in points and steals. He was recognized as a Second-Team [[NJCAA]] Division I All-American and Suncoast Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Keon Ellis Named Second Team NJCAA All-American |url=https://www.fswbucs.com/sports/mbkb/2019-20/releases/20200406ickzq5 |website=Florida Southwestern College Athletics |access-date=November 13, 2021 |date=April 6, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2019-20 Men's Basketball Awards |url=http://thefcsaasports.com/sports/mbkb/2019-20/men-s_basketball_awards |website=NJCAA Region 8 |access-date=November 13, 2021}}</ref> For his junior season, Ellis moved to [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], choosing the Crimson Tide over [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]], [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] and [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Martin |first=Alex |title=FSW guard Keon Ellis commits to Alabama over Iowa State, Kansas State, Western Kentucky |url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/2020/04/16/bama-bound-fsw-guard-keon-ellis-commits-alabama-crimson-tide/2964778001/ |website=[[The News-Press]] |access-date=November 13, 2021 |date=April 16, 2020}}</ref>

He averaged 5.5 points and four rebounds per game as a junior.<ref>{{cite web |last=Casagrande |first=Michael |title=What Keon Ellis brings to Alabama as unheralded guard posts monster stat |url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2021/11/what-keon-ellis-brings-to-alabama-as-unheralded-guard-posts-monster-stat.html |website=AL.com |access-date=November 13, 2021 |date=November 11, 2021}}</ref> Ellis was named to the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Defensive Team as a senior.<ref name=SECAwardsC>{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/33453309/men-basketball-all-sec-teams-awards-announced|title=Men's Basketball All-SEC Teams & Awards Announced |publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |access-date=March 8, 2022}}</ref> He averaged 12.1 points, 6.1 rebounds and two steals per game.<ref>{{cite news |last=Murphy |first=Mark |title=Auburn's Pearl wary of inconsistent but talented Tide |url=https://247sports.com/college/auburn/Article/Auburns-Pearl-wary-of-inconsistent-but-talented-Tide-181920460/ |access-date=March 22, 2022 |work=247 Sports |date=January 31, 2022}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Sacramento / Stockton Kings (2022–2026)===
After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Ellis signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Sacramento Kings]] on July 2, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Sign Neemias Queta And Keon Ellis To Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-neemias-queta-and-keon-ellis-to-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Tucker|title=What Keon Ellis brings to the Sacramento Kings 'He's your classic 3-and-D guy'|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3375884/2022/06/24/keon-ellis-nba-draft/|website=TheAthletic.com|date=June 23, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2024}}</ref> Ellis played in seven total games during the [[2022 NBA Summer League]], averaging 11.4 points on 44.1% shooting from the field and an impressive 46.9% from three, 3.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 2.0 steals per game. He made 16 appearances for Sacramento during his rookie campaign, averaging 1.5 points, 0.5 rebounds, and 0.4 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Keon Ellis 2022-23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4702177/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=March 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On July 2, 2023, Ellis signed another two-way contract with Sacramento<ref>{{cite web|title=Sacramento Kings Re-Sign Keon Ellis to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/sacramento-kings-re-sign-keon-ellis-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2023|access-date=July 2, 2023}}</ref> and on February 9, 2024, he signed a multi-year contract with the Kings.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sacramento Kings Sign Keon Ellis|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/sacramento-kings-sign-keon-ellis|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2024|access-date=February 10, 2024}}</ref> On April 9, Ellis scored a career–high 26 points in a loss against the [[2023–24 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]]. He made 57 appearances (including 21 starts) for the Kings during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging 5.4 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 1.5 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Keon Ellis 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4702177/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=March 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> On April 17, Ellis helped the Kings to a [[NBA play-in tournament|play-in tournament]] victory over the [[2023–24 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]], with 15 points, five assists, four rebounds, three steals and three blocks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rodriguez |first=Tristi |date=2024-04-17 |title=Kings' Ellis puts Warriors, NBA on notice in postseason debut |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/kings-ellis-puts-warriors-nba-225917192.html |access-date=2024-12-15 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

On November 18, 2024, Ellis scored a new career-high 33 points with nine three-pointers in a loss against the [[2024–25 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-18 |title=Keon Ellis scores career high 33 points in Kings 109-108 loss to Hawks - CBS Sacramento |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/keon-ellis-scores-career-high-33-points-in-kings-109-108-loss-to-hawks/ |access-date=2024-12-15 |website=CBS News - Sacramento|agency=Associated Press |language=en-US}}</ref> He made 80 appearances (including 28 starts) for Sacramento in the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]], recording averages of 8.3 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 1.5 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Keon Ellis 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4702177/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=March 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> Ellis played in 43 games (including five starts) for the Kings during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], averaging 5.6 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 0.6 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Keon Ellis 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4702177/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=March 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> During Ellis' tenure with the Kings, the team's fans praised him for his perimeter defense and shooting.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Keon Ellis’ Defense and Shooting Ability Makes Him a Player who Needs To Be on The Floor|url=https://kingsherald.com/articles/keon-ellis-defense-and-shooting-ability-makes-him-a-player-who-needs-to-be-on-the-floor/|website=The Kings Herald|language=en}}</ref>

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2026)===
On February 1, 2026, Ellis was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in a three-team trade that also included the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-01 |title=Cleveland Completes Three-Team Trade with Sacramento and Chicago |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-dennis-schroder-keon-ellis-260201 |access-date=2026-02-01 |website=NBA.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Ellis showcased his defense, hustle and, efforts as he averaged 8.3 points, 1.6 assists, 1.3 steals, and 0.8 block in 29 regular season games with the Cavs. <ref>{{Cite web |date=July 1, 2026 |title=Keon Ellis Regular Season Stats|url=https://www.nba.com/stats/player/1631165?SeasonType=Regular+Season|access-date=July 1, 2026 |website=NBA.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He also made the post-season with the Cavs as he had fallen out of the rotation with only averaging 1.6 points in only 7.4 minutes of playing time. <ref>{{Cite web |date=July 1, 2026 |title=Keon Ellis Playoffs Stats|url=https://www.nba.com/stats/player/1631165?SeasonType=Playoffs|access-date=July 1, 2026 |website=NBA.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2026–present)===
On July 6, 2026, Ellis signed a two-year, $18 million contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 30, 2026 |title=Reports: Keon Ellis to sign two-year deal with Nets |url=https://www.nba.com/news/reports-keon-ellis-nets-deal |access-date=July 6, 2026 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-keon-ellis|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Keon Ellis|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2026}}</ref>
